# B"H
<!-- Boruch Hashem -->
<!-- Blessed is He -->

# Phase Three: Thirty Final Refinements

> May the Awtsmoos renew each test before the browser sings;
> on Awtsmoos.com may truthful paths unfold their wings.

## Third Review

The improved plan identifies the readiness race but still must guard against repairing only the visible exception. The final plan must prove build provenance, URL equivalence, asset existence, scheduler semantics, and deployment behavior as one connected chain.

## Refinements

1. Read settlement code before deciding whether to await it or the raw promise.
2. Preserve the first-paint boundary while awaiting only bootstrap mechanics.
3. Avoid waiting for rich hydration in the essential gate.
4. Assert the scheduler receipt represents installed bootstrap systems.
5. Assert pending rich work is reported as optional, not missing.
6. Test the exact six runtime properties from the console failure.
7. Test scheduler failure propagation without a hanging loading veil.
8. Test rich hydration failure as degraded play.
9. Record runtime stages before and after readiness.
10. Inspect every test fixture’s fake environment timing.
11. Resolve source URLs with real `import.meta.url` examples.
12. Resolve compact URLs with the generated entry URL.
13. Treat dynamic imports as runtime dependencies, not graph omissions.
14. Verify optional modules physically exist at resolved URLs.
15. Ensure no caller duplicates base-path heuristics.
16. Verify query strings survive URL resolution as queries.
17. Verify hashes never become path directories.
18. Locate the exact Chossid file with filesystem evidence.
19. Compare filename case against public routing.
20. Inspect external-asset symlink behavior without following huge trees blindly.
21. Verify model loader fallback does not hide canonical failure.
22. Inspect CompactJS output around each faulty string.
23. Inspect transformer source before proposing a builder edit.
24. Add the smallest fixture that reproduces any builder defect.
25. Run existing CompactJS tests before changing its code.
26. Use full-file rewrites guarded by current hashes.
27. Keep every touched source file below 120 lines or split it.
28. Rebuild rather than hand-edit generated code.
29. Compare source and generated syntax independently.
30. Use a fresh browser load that bypasses stale cache.
31. Capture console errors and failed network requests after boot.
32. Verify movement and at least one bootstrap mechanic interactively.
33. Verify the public route, not merely a local file URL.
34. Update stale entry documentation after code succeeds.
35. Close only when remaining work is empty and evidence is durable.

## Final Decision Standard

A repair is acceptable only when it removes the readiness contradiction at its source, maintains progressive hydration, produces correct URLs in both execution modes, passes focused tests, regenerates cleanly through CompactJS, and survives a real browser reload of the public route.
